title: Frontinus aqueduct source-to-allocation chain with legal scope
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. Frontinus De aquaeductu I.1–2 and II describe each water's source, route and elevation, modules, castella, distributions to public/private uses, reserved imperial supply, and legal limits on drawing water. A finite source-identity chain distinguishes allocation from mere water-name recurrence.

source.work: Frontinus, De aquaeductu urbis Romae, Books I–II
source.source_span: I.1–2 programme and quantities; II distribution through castella, private/public drawing and legal restrictions
source_facts: The report separates source, distance, underground/substructure/arch route and elevation.
It records how much each water distributes outside/inside Rome and how castella feed public works, baths, street basins, Caesar, and private users.
Private users must draw from authorised castella; illicit holes or unlicensed drawing violate the allocation regime.

duplicate_screen.checked: ideas search/duplicates Frontinus aqueduct/allocation/castellum and route-check distribution/source identity
duplicate_screen.difference: No retained card owns this full source-to-route-to-castellum-to-recipient chain; it is a typed distribution mechanism, not a transport lexicon or quantity-only table.

worked_examples: AQUA_X -> ROUTE_X -> CASTELLUM_X -> {PUBLIC_WORKS,PRIVATE_A} with authorised shares
same source identity preserved through a different castellum allocation; unauthorised direct channel yields ILLEGAL_DRAW rather than a new water source
constructor.consequence: A repeated water source can reach different recipients while retaining source identity, and the same recipient can be permitted only through a named castellum. A flat list rival predicts no source/allocation continuity and treats direct illicit diversion as ordinary supply.
constructor.smallest_test: Require two complete distribution records sharing one source but differing in authorised recipient, with one explicit legal exception; test source identity, route stage, and allocation scope jointly.
constructor.rival: Independent inventory of water names, quantities and destinations with no intermediate castellum or legal operator.
assumptions: Quantities are relational capacity fields, not digit meanings.
A source identity persists through routing; this is a source-model convention, not a target claim.
failure_modes: Frontinus is an administrative report whose tables may not encode an executable sequence.
Missing measurements make source and allocation gauges.
A target could reuse forms by register rather than preserving legal scope.

dependencies: Primary Latin/English report is source-owned; no target water gloss or access is proposed.
access: Source-only; no target, reserve, image, experiment, route, ledger, decoder, or root file access.
